g.text: Three-segment trick: one LLM, two losses
Turn a decoder-only LLM into an embedding model without giving up next-token prediction
PART II · GSU SIDE: REASONING ITEM ALIGNMENT
(same LLM; pair from the filtered data)
contrastive loss: pull m and its pair together,
push the other items in the batch away
Training: loss = contrastive (4) + next-token (3), in one pass.
Why: QA sees only <EMB>, so the item information must flow through m.
Use: <EMB> never sees QA, so at inference run input + <EMB> and read m.
QARM V2 (arXiv:2602.08559), §3.1.2, Figure 3. Also: gradient cache for large batches; warm start anneals QA→input attention to 0
